title: Bell Sleeve Wrap Dress Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment Faux-wrap maxi dress with raglan bell sleeves

Level Confident beginner

Sizes US 00 – 22 (XXS – 4XL)

Fabric Crepe knit, scuba crepe, ITY jersey, viscose or matte jersey

Pieces 8

This free wrap dress sewing pattern makes an elegant faux-wrap maxi dress with a crossover V neckline, raglan sleeves that open into wide bell sleeves and a slim column skirt down to the ankle. It is drafted for stretchy knits, so it skims the body and pulls on over the head with only a short invisible zipper at the back neck.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance included on all pieces · 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the skirt and sleeves · invisible zipper 20 cm (8″)

Design details of the bell sleeve wrap dress

Two crossover fronts, each with a short side bust dart, are sewn into a natural waist seam, so the wrap looks real but stays closed all day. The raglan sleeves run from the neckline to the underarm and flare into long bell sleeves that move with every step, and the V neckline is finished with an interfaced facing that continues down the wrap edge to the waist.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the long diagonal line from the shoulder to the waist is the edge of the right front crossing over the left one; the short vertical line inside the neckline is the back zipper seen through the V. The short horizontal lines at the sides are the bust darts, and the curved lines from the neck to the underarm are the raglan seams. The lines inside the right sleeve are only drape folds.

On the back, the long line in the middle is the centre back seam, with the short cross line near the neck marking the end of the zipper. There are no darts at the back and no slit in the skirt.

  • Faux-wrap crossover V neckline, finished with an interfaced facing down to the waist
  • Raglan sleeves flaring into long bell sleeves, with a 2 cm (3/4″) hem
  • Short side bust darts on each front
  • Natural waist seam and a straight ankle-length column skirt
  • Centre back seam with a 20 cm (8″) invisible zipper at the neck

It is a lovely dress for weddings, evening events and festive dinners, and a good step up if you already sew knit tops: you will learn raglan sleeves, a wrap facing and a short invisible zipper in a stretchy fabric.

Sizing guide

Measure your bust around the fullest part and pick the size from the table, then check your waist and hips. This dress is close fitting and drafted for knits: between two sizes, choose by the bust. Not sure how to measure? See how to take body measurements and how to choose your sewing pattern size.

US sizes 00 to 22, drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Letter sizes are a guide only: 00 = XXS · 0–2 = XS · 4–6 = S · 8–10 = M · 12–14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL. Always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished dress measurements

The finished hip is about 1 cm smaller than the body hip: the knit stretch gives the comfort. Lengths are measured at the centre back without seam allowances; the sleeve opening is the full width around the hem of one sleeve.

Fabric amounts

Estimated with every piece laid out single layer for each size, plus about 8 % for shrinkage and straightening. Buy a little more for a one-way print and pre-wash the fabric before cutting. A longer invisible zipper is fine: shorten it from the bottom.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The skirt ends at the ankle. For a midi length, shorten the Skirt Front and both Skirt Backs by the same amount at the hem; the skirt is straight, so nothing else changes. Full guide: how to lengthen or shorten a sewing pattern.

Walking room. The skirt is a slim column. For a longer stride, leave the lower 30 to 40 cm (12 to 16″) of the centre back seam open as a walking slit and topstitch the seam allowances back.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 2.0 to 3.4 m (2 1/4 to 3 3/4 yd) of a medium-weight knit with a soft drape and 25 to 40 % stretch
  • Interfacing: 0.5 m (1/2 yd) of knit (stretch) fusible interfacing for the facings
  • Zipper: one invisible zipper, 20 cm (8″)
  • Thread: polyester all-purpose thread
  • Tools: ballpoint or stretch needle 75 to 80, twin needle for the hems (optional), invisible zipper foot
  • Pins or clips, chalk or a washable marker

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Center Front: cut 2, a left and a right piece
  • 2 Skirt Front: cut 1 on a single layer (drawn whole)
  • 3 Back: cut 2
  • 4 Skirt Back: cut 2
  • 5 Sleeve: cut 2
  • 6 Sleeve Facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing
  • 7 Front Neck Facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing
  • 8 Back Neck Facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing

Choosing fabric for a wrap dress

This dress needs a knit with a good drape and 25 to 40 % crosswise stretch. A crepe knit or scuba crepe gives the smooth, slightly matte look of our emerald version and holds the column skirt nicely; ITY jersey, viscose jersey with elastane and matte jersey are softer and make the bell sleeves swing even more. Ponte also works for a more structured dress.

Woven fabrics are not suitable: the dress has no side zipper and only a short opening at the back neck. More tips in how to choose fabric for sewing patterns and how to sew stretch fabrics.

New to PDF patterns? Start here

Our free step-by-step guides take you from your measurements to a printed pattern:

  1. How to take your body measurements: what to measure and how, in 10 minutes.
  2. How to choose your size: which measurement to follow, and what to do between sizes.
  3. How to print and assemble your pattern: A4 or US Letter, the test box, and taping the pages. Then learn how to read a sewing pattern: symbols and markings explained.

Sewing notes

Fit and style

A close fit through the bodice and hips. Baste the fronts at the waist and try the bodice on before the zipper if you are between sizes.

Fabric

Knits only. Use a ballpoint needle, a stretch stitch or an overlocker, and do not stretch the long wrap edges while sewing.

Zipper

A short invisible zipper at the back neck. See how to sew a zipper.

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, one file per size, US sizes 00 to 22 (XXS to 4XL). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew right sides together with a stretch stitch or an overlocker and press every seam before it is crossed by another one.

  1. Prepare. Fuse knit interfacing to the sleeve facings, front neck facings and back neck facings. Staystitch the long wrap edge of each front, the neck edge of each sleeve and the back neck 8 mm from the edge, without stretching.
  2. Bust darts. Sew the short side bust darts on both fronts, from the side seam to the point, knot the threads and press the darts down.
  3. Bodice side seams. Sew each front to its back at the side seam. You now have a left and a right half of the bodice.
  4. Sleeves. Sew the underarm seam of each sleeve, then hem it: turn up 2 cm (3/4″) and stitch with a twin needle, easing the curve. Set the sleeve into the raglan armhole in one seam, the edge with one notch to the front, two notches to the back.
  5. Neck facing. For each half, join the front neck facing, the sleeve facing and the back neck facing, matching the raglan seams, and finish the outer edge. Sew the facing to the neckline from the waist, up the wrap edge, over the sleeve and to the centre back. Trim, clip, understitch, turn it inside and tack it to the raglan seams.
  6. Cross the fronts. Lap the right front over the left front so the two centre front lines meet at the waist, match the notches and baste across the waist edge.
  7. Zipper and back seam. Insert the 20 cm invisible zipper in the centre back seam from the neck to the ZIP mark, then close the centre back seam down to the waist. Fold the facing ends in and slipstitch them to the zipper tape.
  8. Skirt. Sew the skirt front to the two skirt backs at the side seams, then sew the centre back seam of the skirt from the waist to the hem.
  9. Waist seam. Slip the skirt inside the bodice, right sides together, and match the side seams, the centre back and the point where the fronts cross with the skirt centre front. Stitch, stitch again 6 mm inside and finish.
  10. Hem. Try the dress on, then finish the lower edge, turn up 2 cm (3/4″) and stitch with a twin needle or a narrow zigzag. Give the dress a final press with a pressing cloth.

  • Illustrated diagrams for every step, from the raglan sleeves and the wrap facing to the invisible zipper and the hem
  • Size charts in cm and inches, finished measurements and fabric amounts per size
  • Video guides for the key techniques, with links and QR codes
  • Printable PDF with A0 pattern files, instant download
Shop now

Tips and common mistakes

Wavy wrap edges. The long front edges are cut on a slant and stretch easily. Staystitch them first, add a stay tape if your knit is very soft, and never pull the fabric while you sew the facing.

A neckline that gapes. Baste the crossed fronts at the waist and try the bodice on before you close the back. Understitch the facing as far as you can so it rolls to the inside.

Puckered raglan seams. Match the notches (one at the front, two at the back) and sew with the sleeve on top, letting the machine feed the knit.

A zipper that shows. Press the coil flat from the wrong side, flip the facing out of the way and stitch as close to the teeth as the invisible zipper foot allows.

How to style a wrap dress

Wedding guest: in emerald or burgundy crepe knit with strappy heeled sandals, small gold earrings and a clutch.

Evening: in black matte jersey with a slim belt over the waist seam. For another long silhouette, try our free halter neck maxi dress sewing pattern.

Day: in a soft floral ITY jersey with flat sandals and a denim jacket, or compare it with our free maxi shirt dress sewing pattern for a woven option.

Care

Wash at 30 °C on a gentle cycle, inside out, with the zipper closed. Dry flat or on a hanger, never in the tumble dryer, and press on low heat with a pressing cloth.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every seam and a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the skirt and on the sleeves. The outer edges of the neck facings are only finished.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download has A4 and US Letter files, one file per size, so you only print the size you need.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your bust measurement in the size chart, not by your shop size. The dress is close fitting and made for knits: the finished hip is about 1 cm smaller than the body, which the stretch absorbs. If your fabric has less than 25 % stretch, go one size up.

Is it a real wrap dress?

It is a faux wrap: the two crossover fronts are sewn into the waist seam, so the neckline stays in place, there is nothing to tie and nothing opens. A short invisible zipper at the back neck lets it pull on over the head.

Can I use a woven fabric?

No. With only a short zipper at the back neck, the waist seam has to stretch over the shoulders. Use a knit with 25 to 40 % stretch: crepe knit, scuba crepe, ITY jersey, viscose jersey or matte jersey.

Is this wrap dress hard to sew?

It is a confident-beginner project. There are eight pieces, and you will practise darts, raglan sleeves, a neck facing, crossing the fronts and a short invisible zipper, all in a knit.

Can I make it shorter?

Yes. The pattern is drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in) and ends at the ankle. Shorten the Skirt Front and both Skirt Backs by the same amount at the hem for a midi length.
